before: Some of this is developmental pl/ork you get to do late: making it safe enough for your curiosity and experimenting to finally grow, and your preferences too. It might feel wrong somehow to like something before you've checked anyone's face. You can usually reparent and build who you are at the same time, but if your little one isn't easy to feel yet, making it safe like that is the first phase.

brief:
- notice whether telling the part you've been playing apart from the self that didn't get much practice makes you more curious about both, and better able to relate to them, or more determined to get rid of a "fake" part of yourself
- the aim is a relationship between them inside you that works better, not a new split between an acceptable self and another one that has to disappear
(Context, not for the text: the article has already said, about parts of you that are trying to protect you, "If you treat either one like an enemy, or like proof that something's wrong with you, it'll probably just think 'See? I knew it,' and stay in charge" and "That part doesn't have to move out"; and the parent you inherited calls "anything that does look good" fake. Don't repeat those; this paragraph is about the two selves this section has named: the part you got better at playing, and the self that never had room to form.)
